LESSON: READING 9.2.1 INTENSIVE READING - FICTIONAL AND NON-FICTIONAL

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade six
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: LIFESTYLE DISEASES Suggested Vocabulary cancer, high blood pressure, heart disea
Topic 9.2: Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading - fictional and non-fictional
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading - fictional and non-fictional, part of LIFESTYLE DISEASES Suggested Vocabulary cancer, high blood pressure, heart disea in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade six ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why should we relate events in a text with real life, people or places? 2) How can we predict what will happen in a text or story?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. make connections between events in the text and real-life experiences,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading - fictional and non-fictional in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. create mental images from viewed, heard or read text for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading - fictional and non-fictional in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. respond to texts correctly for comprehension

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading - fictional and non-fictional in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. acknowledge the importance of reading comprehension in lifelong learning. ● Learners with low vision are guided in groups to predict events by studying the title, cover pictures and pictures in a text on lifelong diseases. ● Learners with blindness are guided to predict events by studying the title, listening to picture descriptions of the cover page from the teacher and reading picture descriptions in a text on lifestyle diseases. ● Learner is guided to picture events, characters or places in their minds. ● Learner is guided to read texts of up to 500 words related to the selected theme ● Learner is guided to connect events in a text with an occurrence in their own life or real- world events. ● Learners with low vision are guided to use the images on the front cover to predict events in the text. Learners with blindness are guided in groups to use image descriptions of the front cover given to them by the teacher or sighted peers to predict events in the text. ● Learner is guided to infer the meaning of 1) Why should we relate events in a text with real life, people or places? 2) How can we predict what will happen in a text or story? 55 unfamiliar words and expressions such as fixed phrases, idioms, proverbs and phrasal verbs. ● Learner is guided to retell the events depicted in a text in their own words. ● Learner is guided to answer direct and inferential questions from a variety of texts ● Learners with low vision are guided in groups to create a mind map using words in a text. Learners with blindness are guided in groups to make a summary of the main ideas in a text.

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading - fictional and non-fictional together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.
